title: 138 Awardee Talk: The evaluation of management and protein supplementation strategies on growth and ovarian-follicular parameters in developing beef heifers grazing native rangelands
content:
Abstract
Administration of a pre-weaning growth promoting implant in beef heifers in Southwestern rangelands can improve growth, however the effect of administering a second growth promoting implant after weaning on growth and ovarian parameters is unknown. The objective of these studies was to determine the effect of supplement level when heifers were administered a second Synovex-C implant at weaning on growth and ovarian parameters. In Year 1 (Yr 1) at 2 months of age heifers (N = 17) were assigned to receive one of two implant treatments: 1) Synovex-C implant at 2 months of age (BIMP) or 2) Synovex-C implant at 2 and 8 months of age (WIMP). In Year 2 (Yr 2) at 2 months of age heifers (N = 30) were assigned to receive one of three implant treatments: 1) non-implanted (CON), 2) Synovex-C implant at 2 months of age (BIMP), or 3) Synovex-C implant at 2 and 8 months of age (WIMP). In Yr 1 and 2, at 8 months of age heifers were randomly assigned to one of two supplement levels (High or Low). In Yr 1 and 2, heifers were individually fed supplement three times a week for 25 weeks (High 1.26 kg/hd/d and Low 0.68 kg/hd/d of a 32% CP cube). Bodyweights (BW) were recorded biweekly and grouped in 4 periods (weeks 0, 2-4, 6-14, and 16-25). At the end of the supplementation period heifers underwent bilateral ovariectomies. Weight, height, and length of each ovary was recorded. Length of the largest follicle was recorded and follicular fluid (FF) was collected for analysis of estradiol and progesterone concentrations. Statistical analyses remain separated between years due to having a CON implant treatment for Yr 2. Ovarian and follicular measurements were analyzed using MIXED procedures in SAS. Average daily gain (ADG) and BW were analyzed as repeated measures using MIXED procedures in SAS. In Yr 1, implant, supplement level, and implant × supplement level did not affect heifer BW (P ≥ 0.64). In Yr 2, implant × supplement level tended to influence heifer BW (P = 0.09) with High BIMP heifers tending to have elevated BW compared to Low BIMP heifers. In Yr 1, implant, supplement level, and their interaction did not influence ovarian weight, length, or height (P ≥ 0.16). In Yr 2, High heifers had increased ovarian length compared to Low heifers (P = 0.03) and WIMP heifers tended to have increase ovarian length (P = 0.09) compared to CON. In Yr 2, High heifers tended to have decreased largest follicle diameter compared to Low heifers (P = 0.09). In conclusion, administration of second Synovex-C implant at weaning did not enhance growth performance, however supplementing increased protein may hinder follicular parameters.
